einzeiler: How Russia exploits a rift between Washington and Kyiv to freeze Ukrainian cities.
kurzfassung: As U.S.-Ukraine relations deteriorate following a diesel trade deal, Russia has escalated its bombing campaign against Ukrainian cities. Moscow aims to cripple the country's energy infrastructure ahead of winter, leaving millions facing severe shortages of heat, water, and power. Meanwhile, Ukraine struggles with a critical shortage of air defense interceptors and disruptions to satellite communication and early-warning intelligence.
stichpunkte: A recent diesel deal between Washington and Moscow triggered a sharp public rift between President Trump and President Zelensky.
Russia has intensified its aerial bombardments, deploying hundreds of drones and ballistic missiles in unprecedented nighttime attacks.
The introduction of fast, jet-powered drones has made it significantly harder for Ukrainian forces to defend urban centers.
Ukraine intercepts only about 10 percent of incoming ballistic missiles due to a severe shortage of U.S.-supplied Patriot interceptors.
A leaked Russian war plan reveals a strategy to cut off electricity, heating, and water supplies in major cities by up to 90 percent.
Frontline operations have been complicated by disruptions to StarShield satellite internet access.
Brief lapses in U.S. intelligence sharing have left civilians with almost no warning before ballistic missile impacts.
While the campaign may not force total capitulation, it threatens to weaken Ukraine permanently ahead of future negotiations.
beschreibung:
President Trump said he was making an energy deal with President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia and waiving new sanctions on Moscow. Now, he’s feuding with Ukraine’s leader, Volodymyr Zelensky.
Russia is taking advantage of the moment by relentlessly striking Kyiv, killing civilians and cutting off power for more than a million people.
Constant Méheut, who is covering the war for The New York Times, explains why Mr. Putin appears so confident that Russia can bomb Ukraine into submission.
Guest: Constant Méheut, a correspondent covering the war in Ukraine for The New York Times.
Background reading:
Analysis: Why Russia sees a window to bomb Ukraine into submission.
Mr. Zelensky says Mr. Trump risks a “historic mistake” if he backs Russia.
